articles.title: A'ja Wilson named WNBA MVP for third consecutive year, fifth time overall as Aces star extends all-time record
articles.summary: Wilson extends her WNBA record for most MVP Awards.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces star forward A'ja Wilson has been named the 2026 WNBA MVP.

The WNBA announced the news on Thursday.

Wilson received 65 of 74 first-place votes and 713 points from a panel of WNBA media. WNBA Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles of the Minnesota Lynx finished second in voting (six first-place votes, 442 points).

Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell (two first-place votes, 287 points), Fever guard Caitlin Clark (one first-place vote, 212 points) and Liberty forward Breanna Stewart (171 points) finished in third through fifth place, respectively.

Wilson played in 41 games this season. She averaged 26.2 points per game, the second-highest mark of her career, and the highest in the WNBA this year.

The forward also averaged 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.9 blocks per game.

Here is a look at how Wilson stacked up with the other MVP finalists.

Wilson has now won the award three years in a row, and this is the fifth overall MVP award in what is assuredly a Hall of Fame career. The Aces forward was already in the conversation among the greatest basketball players ever, and this latest honor only adds to her lore.

Across the NBA and WNBA, only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (6) has more MVPs. Wilson's fifth ties her with Michael Jordan and Bill Russell. Wilson already held the WNBA record for most MVP Awards with four, after she surpassed Sheryl Swoopes, Lisa Leslie and Lauren Jackson, who each won three, last year.

Wilson's career accolades are almost unbelievable when you break them down. The 2026 season was just her ninth year in the league, and she's now been named the MVP in more than half of the seasons she has played.

The Aces forward has already won three WNBA championships and has been named WNBA Finals MVP twice.

Wilson has also been a three-time WNBA Defensive Player of the Year, eight-time All-Star, three-time scoring champion, and six-time blocks leader.

articles.title: 2026-27 NBA Season Preview: Lakers, Suns, Clippers, Warriors, Kings (Pacific Division)
articles.summary: Let's break down what to like and be concerned about, a lineup to watch and a reasonable range for them to finish in the standings.
articles.body:
With the regular season set to tip off on Oct. 20, let's take a look at where each team in the Pacific Division stands. We'll break down what to like and be concerned about, a lineup to watch and a reasonable range for them to finish in the standings.

Previous divisions: Central • Southwest • Northwest

WHAT TO LIKE: Luka Dončić + Austin Reaves

With LeBron James in Philadelphia, the Lakers have officially turned things over to Luka Dončić and, to a lesser-but-still-important extent, Austin Reaves.

Dončić is a perennial MVP candidate who looks poised for another fantastic season. Reaves is coming off the best season of his career, firmly establishing himself as one of the most dynamic offensive players in the league.

Both put a tremendous amount of pressure on defenses with their ability to get downhill for finishes, draw fouls, and make plays for others. Dončić, of course, is one of the best passers of all time; certainly a complement to his elite scoring chops.

The Lakers scored often and efficiently in the minutes Dončić and Reaves shared without LeBron last year; I'd expect that to continue.

While the price was steep, Walker Kessler should help this defense quite a bit. They've long needed someone who could protect the rim and clean the glass at a high level; he should be able to do just that.

The first Sandro Mamukelashvili grab-and-go is going to hit like [redacted]. In all seriousness, a dribble-pass-shoot 4 should vibe nicely with this group, and take some of the creation burden off of Dončić or Reaves whenever they share the floor.

I'm fascinated by the wing options the Lakers can cycle through in general, but I'm very "in" on the Cameron Carr experience. He has to get stronger, but that's just a blend of shooting and athleticism that I believe in.

I believe Kessler will help, and I like the attempts the Lakers made to address some of their perimeter woes (Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams in particular).

It's been fascinating to watch them tap the "high pick-up points" button so far in preseason, and it'll be cool to track what their blend of switching vs. more traditional coverages will be.

Ultimately, they won't hit their ceiling as a team if the defense can't get to a certain level. Could be 18th, could be 15th — I just don't think they can be a bottom-10 unit and get to where they want to go.

This is still a team that lacks athleticism, at least compared to the West's elite (OKC, SAS, MIN). It's not impossible to overcome, but it's worth monitoring what this looks like in high-wattage matchups.

While I ultimately think they can handle it, there is so much initiation responsibility on Dončić and Reaves. They'll spread it around with Mamu and others at times, but the drop-off is pretty substantial.

Who is the starting 4 for this group? I'd rather have Mamu as a change-of-pace option instead of a locked-in starter. You're asking for spacing problems if you roll with Jarred Vanderbilt, though he could help boost the defense. Do you toss an additional wing into the mix to lock in Dončić as the nominal 4 defensively? We'll see where Mr. Redick lands.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Quentin Grimes-Thybulle-Reaves-Dončić-Kessler

Don't be thrown off by the order this group is listed in. This would still be Dončić and Reaves handling most of the initiation duties; Reaves would be defending the worst opposing perimeter player, while Dončić would be the nominal 4 (a pretty common thing as is, anyway).

The Lakers will be mixing and matching different defensive trios around the Dončić-Reaves pairing all year. I'm particularly interested in this one: the solid on-ball chops of Quentin Grimes, S-tier event creation from Thybulle, and the sturdy rim protection of Kessler.

This could earnestly — some may argue "finally" — be the MVP year for Dončić. There's best-offense-in-the-league potential with this group with him and Reaves at the helm, plus a higher volume of quality role players that could slot in alongside them. If the defense is better than expected, there's a pathway to churning out a ton of wins.

Because of how vital Dončić and Reaves are to their offense, the Lakers can't really afford to lose either of them for an extended period.

You could make a similar argument for Kessler and the defense. Anything short of an elite offense and serviceable defense could leave them vulnerable to the play-in picture.

The Suns were one of my favorite teams to watch last year, largely because of how they went about things defensively.

It started early with high pick-up points, then continued within half-court possessions with their mix of ball pressure, off-ball activity, and willingness to send double teams to worthy adversaries.

Dillon Brooks returns to set the tone — it took him precisely one (1) preseason game to remind folks that he's here for any and all nonsense — and guard at an All-Defense level. Collin Gillespie (great new contract) will be part of the full-court pressure package. Jordan Goodwin (another great contract), Ryan Dunn, and Rasheer Fleming bring a collective chaos off the bench.

I imagine this is still going to be a team that really bothers people.

New jersey number, same beast. Devin Booker remains one of the best and most versatile offensive players we have in the league, able to oscillate between on- and off-ball usage. It feels so weird to say we're entering Year 12 with him.

People should already be familiar with Oso Ighodaro based on his work last year, but I think he's primed for a better, louder campaign. Honestly, between him and Khaman Maluach, I feel pretty good about the Suns' center room moving forward.

I mentioned him in the initial defense section, but I don't know if I could be a bigger fan of Jordan Goodwin than I am. Fantastic defender, crafty offensive rebounder and screener, and a guy that quietly shot 37.1% on over four attempts from deep last year. He's a winning player.

BIGGEST QUESTION MARK: Are teams more prepared for them?

I'm not sure teams were ready for how aggressively the Suns were going to play. Their backcourt pressure and emphasis on crashing the offensive glass was a lot to deal with. They bombed away from 3 (sixth in 3-point rate, 11th in percentage) on top of that.

They're not going to surprise anyone this year, so what does that look like? Are teams more dutiful about boxing out? Do we see a higher level of switching from teams to limit the Suns' shot quality — something we saw signs of in the second half of last year?

I'm curious about what Year 2 of the Jordan Ott experience looks like.

On the high end, Jalen Green can take pressure off Booker and others with his ability to score in bunches. We've already seen glimpses of him taking advantage of tilted defenses playing off of Booker's gravity. On the low end, his decision-making can go haywire, and teams are comfortable putting him in action on the other end. I wonder how much Green will have to prove he should be part of this core moving forward.

Tied to that, I'm slightly underwhelmed by the collective passing ability on the roster. Scheme and spacing can go a long way toward simplifying reads, but this feels like something that will pop up against the league's best (or at least most aggressive) defenses.

How much Mark Williams are we going to get this year? I enjoyed him when he played last season — he really made strides defensively, even mixing in some late switches when asked — but he's already slated to miss much of the season as he recovers from shoulder surgery. A shame, really.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Gillespie-Booker-Brooks-Dunn-Maluach

We haven't seen much of this group — +6 in 11 minutes last year, +3 in two minutes in their preseason opener against the Pistons — but it's easy to see why and how this unit would work with more time.

A healthy amount of shooting and creation between Gillespie, Booker, and Brooks; plenty of defense between Gillespie (at least to be annoying at the POA), Brooks and Dunn, plus whatever rim protection Maluach can provide on top of that as he grows more comfortable. Oh, and you can't forget the offensive rebounding you could get from three, if not four spots.

A strong foundation was established last year, particularly on the defensive end. What if the young trio of Dunn/Fleming/Maluach each take steps within that context?

Booker was quite good last year without shooting particularly well from deep; what does a bounceback year look like for him, in addition to everything he already does well?

A sturdy defense, another year of winning the possession battle (crushing the offensive glass, forcing turnovers), internal development, and another All-NBA level campaign from Booker could have the Suns firmly in the playoff picture.

This could simply be some combination of the league being more prepared for how the Suns want to guard, some scoring regression from Brooks, missing the 3-point shooting they sent out the building this summer, and other teams in the 7-11 range being more competitive.

WHAT TO LIKE: Darius Garland at the helm

We finally get a taste of Darius Garland as the unquestioned orchestrator of a team. He pairs elite pull-up chops with a yo-yo dribble and top-tier passing ability. If the preseason opener was any indication, the pace and tempo should be up for the Clippers compared to last year.

(A quick note: the Clippers haven't finished inside the top-15 in pace since the 2019-20 season. Their only finish inside the top-20 during this span came in 2021-22, when they finished 19th.)

In general, I'm amused by the young talent on this roster. I'm excited to see more of Keaton Wagler, mostly tracking his progress as a driver against more set defenses. Did you know Yanic Konan Niederhäuser averaged 11 & 8 in the games he logged 20+ minutes in last year? Now you do. His screening and hub work moved me to the point I made sure to ask him about it during All-Star festivities last year. I thought Kobe Sanders had an underrated All-Rookie campaign on a team that mattered; really, I enjoyed the minutes from him and Jordan Miller (if 27 counts as "young" still) last year.

Any year I get to watch Kris Dunn hound people on defense is a year that I'm personally thankful for. Regardless of how good or bad the Clippers end up being, don't take his work for granted. I'll be locked in during the minutes he and Derrick Jones Jr. share the floor.

I thought snagging Rui Hachimura from across the street was a good bit of business from the Clippers this offseason. They could certainly use all the shooting they can get, and it's felt like he hasn't missed a spot-up 3 in two years.

I'm still trying to wrap my head around acquiring Brandon Ingram and discovering a partially torn Achilles. It's also worth monitoring the health of Garland's toe — an odd thing to have to type, but an important subplot nonetheless. In today's "No, duh" portion of the program, it's less than ideal when your two best players may be hindered or unavailable.

I'm excited about the young big man room, but Brook Lopez is still the best rim protector (and screener!) of the bunch. Can he produce enough on both ends to serve as a bridge, or are we truly nearing the end with him?

It's another team for Ingram, but it's truly a new beginning for trade partner Gradey Dick. Dick has underwhelmed as a 3-point shooter in his young career (34.3% on 4.0 attempts), which puts a cap on some of the ancillary skills he does possess (don't sleep on the passing chops). Here's hoping he's able to find his footing in L.A.

The Clippers were one of the worst rebounding teams in the league last year, ranking 23rd in offensive rebound rate and 25th in defensive rebound rate. I look at this roster and find myself #whelmed by the personnel on that front. They've got to find, or limit, an edge on the glass somewhere to raise their floor.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Garland-Wagler-Miller-Sanders-Konan Niederhäuser

Call me basic for wanting to see Garland plus the young guys, but … I do want to see Garland plus the young guys.

There's shooting, there's secondary creation, there's cutting. There is so much space for Garland-YKN pick-and-rolls to operate within; even outside of this lineup, I would not be surprised if I pull up Second Spectrum a couple of months into the season and see that they're one of the best pick-and-roll combos in the league.

There's enough juice here to be annoying, especially if they get 60+ games out of Garland and Ingram. In theory, you have a high-end initiator in Garland and a quality failsafe in Ingram. A cast of role players and youngsters that can shoot and beat tilted defenses could vibe well with them.

Get enough defensive buy-in overall — lord knows head coach Ty Lue is going to ask for it — and I wouldn't be totally shocked by a high 30s/low 40s win total.

If Garland and/or Ingram miss substantial time, this could be a really rough group in the half-court. I'd worry a little about Wagler being overburdened in a context like that, though you could argue those reps could pay off down the road.

WHAT TO LIKE: Stephen Curry, still magical

It may feel like an empty platitude sometimes, but you truly do have to appreciate greatness when it's in front of you. Stephen Curry is an all-time great, a few steps above your typical future Hall-of-Famers. We've never had someone warp the floor like he does; even at this stage of his career, no one strikes the same level of " where did he go???" fear like Curry.

Cherish the deep pull-ups. Cherish the possessions where he's standing off the ball, slouched over, with a defender draped on him, only for him to jog to a spot before breaking into a dead sprint and creating chaos. Cherish the mindmeld he's developed with Draymond Green, and the two-man magic those two can still create.

Death, taxes, and the Warriors running some variation of Split action. You can set your clock to it. No matter what kind of shifts we may see to their early flow, that will (and should!) remain a half-court staple.

Yaxel Lendeborg profiles as a forward who can do a little bit of everything, and I'm naturally drawn to those types of players. It's been fun watching his aggression perk up as Summer League and now preseason play has raged on. On a lighter note, the jovial back-and-forths with Green — the Michigan vs. Michigan State rivalry will never die — have made me laugh since he's been drafted.

It's a niche point for people outside of the Warriors fan base, but I'm here for another year of Gary Payton II shaking loose as a screener and short-roll playmaker off the bench.

It's a boring one, but I don't know if there's a team in the division whose floor and ceiling relies on reasonable health as much as the Warriors do.

Curry has missed at least 10 games in four of the past five seasons, and is coming off a 43-game campaign. Green is in the same four-of-five boat as Curry. Jimmy Butler is already slated to miss a big chunk of the season as he recovers from last year's ACL injury. Nobody knows the status of Kristaps Porziņģis right now as he continues to battle through an illness. Even on the younger side, there's no telling when Moses Moody will make his return either.

There is top-end talent and depth to like on this roster, but it simply won't matter if they're not healthy enough to string wins together.

In light of the offense potentially shifting a bit, I am getting increasingly worried about Green's fit within it. We saw him ramp up his 3-point volume to career-high levels last season (4.6 attempts), but he shot well below league average (32.6%). Not only is Green still a quality passing hub, they kinda need that usage to offset his limitations as a scorer. We'll see what kind of balance is struck.

While Butler (and Porziņģis) are out, there is a massive drop-off between Curry and the next best creator. I think Podz is a tad underrated, and in a surprise to no one who's followed my work, I'm a fan of the Brandon Williams experience. The prospect of those guys being next-best options on a team with serious aspirations is a bit unfair to everyone involved.

It ties into their obvious size issues, but the Warriors were one of the worst defensive rebounding teams in the league (24th in defensive rebound rate). I'm not sure how much better that'll be this year. I'm a little concerned by how much they may need to force turnovers to offset that.

LINEUP TO WATCH: Curry-Podziemski-Melton-Lendeborg-Green

In general, I'm fascinated by how often the Warriors will lean into lineups with Green at the 5. His workload will have to be managed if there's any hope of making playoff noise, but the offense undoubtedly opens up more in smaller groups.

We only got 43 minutes of the Curry/Podziemski/Melton/Green quartet last season, but they did win those minutes by a whopping 33 points. Adding Lendeborg into that group as a versatile two-way piece sounds like a good time to me .

If Curry's healthy, he's shown that he's still All-NBA good. Green can still defend at a high level, even if he can't quite hit his DPOY-level peaks as long. There's a foundation on both ends where, if you get enough contributions from the youngsters and versatile role pieces, they could churn out enough wins to stay in the play-in picture.

If they have Butler and Porziņģis back by the time the play-in rolls around, they'd be a team much more dangerous than their 7-10 seeding would suggest.

WORST CASE: Outside of the Play-In Tournament

The core is good but aging. Another injury-riddled season — or even one where some understandable slippage from the vets happens (or continues) — could leave them on the outside looking in.

I wrote about it earlier this summer , but Darius Acuff just moves like a guy who knows he belongs. Slick handle, a fearless creator inside the arc, an audacious one outside of it. He feels like the most obvious "18 & 6 on 52 TS" rookie of all time, but it'll be fun to track his Year 1 journey.

This is a fun cast of young players, even if there isn't an obvious blue-chipper in the group. I didn't have Keegan Murray turning into one of the more underrated wing/forward defenders in the league, but he has that plus theoretical shooting chops (I'm starting to get worried ) going for him. Nique Clifford is my kind of dime-tossing, gap-filling wing and I hope he gets more put on his plate this year. I enjoyed the center duo of Maxime Raynaud and energy-on-1000 backup Dylan Cardwell last year; boy, will they need the latter's rim protection this year. Emanuel Sharp will take your lunch and help you look for it.

For however long he's on the roster, Domantas Sabonis will provide a level of half-court stability that this team will need. He's one of the best handoff hubs and screen-setters in the league; it took a singular preseason game to get a glimpse into how helpful he can be for Acuff specifically.

As one of, what feels like, the few public Ben Simmons defenders left, I'm happy that he's in a better place. I'm also glad he's going to be on a basketball court again; if nothing else, the stakes will be low, and he has plenty of scoring guards to flow into handoffs or ball screens with.

BIGGEST QUESTION MARK: Defensive consistency

There are some fun defenders on the roster — namely Sharp, Murray, and Cardwell — but I expect this to be one of the worst units in the league. I do wonder what base they'll ultimately land on — Sabonis' presence on the roster plus their early preseason film suggests they'll be an at-the-level unit — and if they can build some good habits this year.

How long are Sabonis and Zach LaVine (please get him on a good team) going to be here? Both can be useful; I talked about Sabonis earlier, and LaVine's ability to shoot, drive, and generally soak up usage should take some pressure off of Acuff. Bigger picture, I wonder what kind of deals can be found for them.

Somewhat related: as Acuff is a rookie, he's absolutely going to have moments where he's a little too gunsling-y. Who's the guard stabilizer on this team? LaVine can soak up the scoring burden, but I certainly don't want him initiating a bunch of offense if I can help it. Is it going to be Clifford by default? Is this going to wind up being Elfrid Payton at some point this year?

On the other side of my Simmons excitement: Who, exactly, is going to be his frontcourt partner? Are we seeing any minutes with him at the 5? They technically have the forwards (Murray, De'Andre Hunter) to make that alignment kinda work — Murray's a not-so-sneakily good shot-blocker — but how often will that button be pressed?

LINEUP TO WATCH: Acuff-Clifford-Hunter-Murray-Sabonis

I don't know if head coach Doug Christie has the stomach to roll out All Youth lineups in games of consequence, hence Sabonis being here instead of Raynaud.

There's room for Acuff to cook a bit with Clifford operating as a secondary. You can move Murray and Hunter around the board instead of simply spacing them. And if all else fails, you have Sabonis as the proverbial (All-Star) adult in the room to bring some direction in the half-court.

I will take no comments on the defense, though Clifford/Hunter/Murray could provide enough juice to make the group close to serviceable.

BEST CASE: Outside of the Play-In + sense of direction

This is the outcome that features an earnest Rookie of the Year push from Acuff, plus notable strides made from young guys like Murray, Clifford, and Raynaud. This is also the world where they're able to find reasonable deals for at least two of Sabonis, LaVine and Malik Monk, clearing the way (and the books, as that matters) for the team to truly lean into this phase of the rebuild.

An entertaining-but-inefficient year from Acuff that leads to even more arguments from Draft Twitter. Plateauing from the Year 2 cast. LaVine and others wasting away on this team. More unease and angst surrounding the stability of Christie's job. The Kings landing near the bottom of the standings wouldn't be inherently bad; coming out of this season feeling directionless would be a failure.

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers vs. Brooklyn Nets Live NBA Preseason Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: The revamped Philadelphia 76ers travel to Barclays Center Thursday night to take on the Brooklyn Nets at 7:30 p.m EST in what will be each team's second game of the preseason. And guess what?!
articles.body:
The revamped Philadelphia 76ers travel to Barclays Center Thursday night to take on the Brooklyn Nets at 7:30 p.m EST in what will be each team's second game of the preseason. And guess what?!

We're getting our first look at Philly's starting five of LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid!

Naturally, then, this exhibition tilt is dripping with implications. The biggest storylines and questions we will be following throughout include:

How does the Sixers' newly unveiled starting five fare? Philly is attempting to join together a bunch of ball-dominant forces. Even if you're unbothered by the dynamic, this is a huge undertaking. The first glimpse at how they work alongside one another will be fascinating.

How many minutes do Philly's starters play? We typically get to see them through the first half. But LeBron is battling chronic arthritis in his left foot as well as sciatica. Embiid is also Embiid. Head coach Nick Nurse may opt to limit their court time even more than usual.

The Sixers' center rotation. New addition Ariel Hukporti suffered a ruptured right Achilles tendon in Philly's preseason opener while Adem Bona (left foot), Dominick Barlow (back) and Tacko Fall (left hip) remain sidelined with their own injuries. After Embiid, we should brace ourselves for minutes with Jabari Walker, Dean Wade and even LeBron at the 5.

The Nets' center rotation. Day'Ron Sharpe has been ruled out with left shoulder soreness. Mo Wagner is the only other conventional center on the roster, so we should see some Julius Randle and Danny Wolf in the middle.

Keep up with all the highlights, analysis, commentary and storylines that emerge through this one below.

Multiple imaginary sources confirm LeBron will be sending Embiid straight to bed after the game without any dessert.

LeBron now has more no-look assists (two) than appearances in a Sixers uniform (one).

Labaron Philon Jr. Might've Been a Steal

This is the second straight game Labaron Philon Jr. has looked ultra-comfortable working away from the ball. And he's also got plenty of derring-do on it.

With all due respect to Anfernee Simons, Philly's rookie might need to get actual minutes this season.

The Sixers' New Era is Officially 12 Minutes Old

Biggest takeaways for the Sixers from that first quarter:

Both Maxey and VJ Edgecombe remain fast.

LeBron James can still control the game with his passing.

Opposing teams are not going to shy away from attacking Joel Embiid.

Score: Nets 33, Sixers 33 | End of the first quarter

The Nets Have Some On-Ball Speed of Their Own

We won't even mention the Sixers' interior defense. Instead, it's your move, VJ Edgecombe.

The Joel Embiid Experience So Far Has Been Uneven

Embiid putting the clamps on a speedster like Nolan Traoré is a good sign. But the Nets are relentlessly attacking him, like he's supposed to be the weak point of Philly's defense. That's something to monitor moving forward.

The ball movement. LeBron's no-look bounce pass. Edgecombe's baseline cut.

Zero field-goal attempts for LeBron halfway through first quarter is actually insane. Then again, the Sixers have more than enough scoring . Maybe this is a sign of things to come.

Totally unrelated: Anybody got odds on LeBron leading the league in assists per game this season?

Egor Dëmin just made LeBron look his age. And maybe even older.

Score: Sixers 15, Nets 15 | 6:37 remaining in the first quarter

It feels fitting that LeBron's first assist with the Sixers not only went to VJ Edgecombe, but came on a transition bucket following a Nets make .

Translation: This Philly team is going to run.

OK, watching shaved-head LeBron do this in a Sixers jersey is objectively weird. Still cool. But weird.

LeBron Gets a Warm Welcome in His First Sixers Start

Important note: This game is taking place in Brooklyn. LOL.

The Scoring in Philly's Starting 5 is Unreal

On the one hand, that's a lot of points. On the other hand, tHeRe Is OnLy OnE bAlL.

Joel Embiid is the 76ers' Only Healthy Center

Get ready to play center, LeBron. And Dean Wade. And Jabari Walker.

The Nets' Starting Lineup is Something...

Projected starters Mikel Brown Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe are both out, but even so, running with Julius Randle or Noah Clowney as your de facto small forward is certainly a choice.

The Vibes are Immaculate in Philly's Locker Room

No matter how old you are or where your NBA loyalties lie, don't you dare for a second feel sheepish if you're stoked to see Philly's starting five in action.

Case in point: Even the Sixers organization can't contain their excitement. They're basically that six-year-old staying up to catch a glimpse of Santa Claus on Christmas Eve.

We know who's in the Sixers' starting five. But something about seeing it typed out on screen makes it somehow feel more surreal and ridiculous.

The 76ers' New-Look Starting Lineup is Ready 🍿

Everybody will surely have a measured reaction to how LeBron, Embiid, Maxey, Brown and Edgecombe fare during their first live-game stint together.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Gets 1 WNBA MVP 1st Place Vote, Where Did Angel Reese, Bueckers Finish in Voting?
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark received her first-ever WNBA regular-season MVP first-place vote, per the league's reveal of this year's voting results.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark received her first-ever WNBA regular-season MVP first-place vote, per the league's reveal of this year's voting results.

Clark finished fourth overall for the award, which Las Vegas center A'ja Wilson won for a record fifth time.

Dallas Wings guard Paige Bueckers got three third-place votes en route to a sixth-place finish, and Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese received four fourth-place votes and ended seventh.

Clark, who also finished fourth in the MVP race during her 2024 rookie season, averaged a career-high 22.3 points (third in the league), 8.3 assists (second in the WNBA) and 4.0 rebounds per game. Indiana cruised to a playoff spot with a 28-16 record but lost a hard-fought first-round series to the defending WNBA champion Aces.

Bueckers made the All-Star Game for the second time in as many seasons, posting 20.9 points on 51.2 percent shooting (41.0 percent from three), 5.9 assists and 4.1 rebounds. She helped Dallas improve from 10 to 27 wins, earning a playoff spot. The Wings pushed the No. 2 seed Golden State Valkyries to three games but fell in the first round.

Reese arrived in Atlanta after being traded from the Chicago Sky, and she helped the Dream win 30 games for the second consecutive year. This season's Defensive Player of the Year averaged 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game. The Dream finished second in defensive rating . Atlanta is currently one win away from making the WNBA Finals after going up 2-0 in its semifinal series with the New York Liberty.

articles.title: El Valencia sólo sabe ganar en la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Derrota al Hapoel para igualar su mejor arranque histórico en la competición
articles.summary: Derrota al Hapoel para igualar su mejor arranque histórico en la competición
articles.body: Un sólido Valencia Basket, guiado por TJ Shorts y Kam Taylor, controló este jueves de principio a fin al Hapoel Tel Aviv y sumó su cuarta victoria de la temporada en otras tantas jornadas de la Euroliga, en la que se mantiene como único equipo invicto junto al poderoso Panathinaikos. El conjunto valenciano se había puesto como uno de sus objetivos mejorar su entrada en el choque y fue ese impulso inicial el que le permitió llevar la iniciativa y aguantar los envites del equipo israelí, que contó con una gran actuación de Antonio Blakeney. Además, si bien no consiguió ganar la competición del rebote, otro de sus objetivos, la igualó al máximo. Ambos equipos mostraron de inicio sus cartas más evidentes, la capacidad de anotar de tres por parte de los locales, que abrieron el partido con cuatro triples, y la mayor fortaleza interior por parte de los visitantes, que se nutrieron de los puntos de Zach Leday. Como de tres en tres se suma más rápido, las primeras ventajas fueron para el Valencia (18-8, m.4). Tras un oportuno descanso, el regreso de un escurridizo TJ Shorts y un aceptable control del rebote permitió a los locales atacar en velocidad al Hapoel. Además la buena defensa de Gonzalo Corbalán sobre Micic y de Josep Puerto sobre Bryant dejó al equipo israelí sin sus recursos más obvios en caso de problemas y la renta local se estiró (41-27, m.16). Pero al Valencia se le hizo larga la primera parte. Un par de triples de Ish Wainright mantuvieron enganchado al Hapoel y otros dos de Blakeney, que ya venía de sumar dos previamente, le permitieron llegar al descanso con su desventaja reducida a la mitad (47-40, m.20). En la reanudación, Blakeney siguió anotando y el Hapoel logró rebajar el ritmo del choque, pero el Valencia resistió gracias a los puntos que rascaron sus interiores. Dieron tiempo a que regresara el certero Puerto, que con dos triples seguidos dejó en nada el trabajo de su rival y llevó la renta local de nuevo a los catorce puntos. El Hapoel acusó el golpe. Perdió mordiente en defensa y fe en el rebote de ataque y el cubano Jasiel Rivero supo rematar algunas acciones ofensivas para llevar la ventaja cerca de los veinte puntos y poner a prueba la dureza mental del Hapoel (74-55, m.30). No se rindió el equipo israelí, que aprovechó la relajación defensiva del Valencia para meter algunas canastas y recuperar terreno. Los puntos de Taylor sostuvieron a los locales pero el partido ya no parecía estar decidido. Cuando más perdido parecía estar Armoni Brooks, el exterior estadounidense encadenó un triple y un 'dos más uno' que dieron aire al Valencia aunque no soluciones estables. El Hapoel fue aumentado la presión y Xavi Albert recurrió a la experiencia de Mirotic para tratar de calmar a los suyos y compensar el regreso de Blakeney. Pero fue TJ Shorts quien cerró el choque. Anotó un tiro libre tras provocar una falta, le sacó otra en ataque en la jugada siguiente a Satoransky y asistió a Osetkowski para que anotara el triple que acabó con la esperanza israelí. 93.- Valencia Basket (29+18+27+19): TJ Shorts (15), Brooks (9), Taylor (17), Osetkowski (10), Sako (2) -cinco titular- Cárdenas (-), Moore (4), Corbalán (-), Puerto (11), Rivero (10), Mirotic (9) y Reuvers (6). 82.- Hapoel Tel Aviv (17+23+17+25): Satoransky (4), Micic (4), Bryant (12), Leday (7), Oturu (6) -cinco titular- German (-), Blakeney (30), Wainright (6), Toppin (5), Odiase (8) y Caboclo (-). Árbitros: Hordov (CRO), Zamojski (POL) y Boubert (FRA). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el Roig Arena de València ante 10.850 espectadores.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson Reacts to Winning Historic 5th WNBA MVP Award, Learned News from Kamala Harris
articles.summary: Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson was named the WNBA MVP on Thursday for the fifth time, the most in the history of the league.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces superstar A'ja Wilson was named the WNBA MVP on Thursday for the fifth time, the most in the history of the league.

And she received the news from a very special messenger—former Vice President Kamala Harris:

As for the achievement, Wilson spoke about maintaining an MVP-worthy level of play.

"The crown gets heavy," she told reporters . "Wearing it gets heavy. It may tilt, it may slip, but my biggest thing is making sure it doesn't fall—and it doesn't just necessarily mean the crown falls on me, but it doesn't fall on anyone that may be wearing it... if you're going to wear the crown, if you're going to rock it, you've got to have an understanding that its going to get heavy. But it doesn't mean it's going to drop. Not on my watch."

Wilson, 30, has now been the MVP in five of the last seven WNBA seasons. No other player in league history has more than three. Her career accolades also include three WNBA titles, a Rookie of the Year award, three Defensive Player of the Year awards, eight All-Star Game appearances and five first-team All-WNBA nods.

Wilson's dominance cannot be denied. She led the WNBA in scoring (26.2 PPG), was fifth in rebounding (9.4 RPG), first in blocks (1.9 BPG), tied for 12th in steals (1.4 SPG) and shot an impressive 52.7 percent from the field and 40.4 percent from three.

The MVP voting wasn't even close, nor should it have been:

Per ESPN's Michael Voepel , Wilson became the first player in WNBA history to average 25 or more points points per game wh0ile shooting at least 50 percent from the field and 40 percent from three, and the only player who has ever averaged more points in a season than Wilson did this year was... herself, back in 2024 (26.4 PPG).

At this point—and with all apologies to Diana Taurasi—the GOAT debate in women's basketball may be settled.

"Like I've said, 'Take her off Mount Rushmore, she's Everest,'" Aces head coach Becky Hammon told Voepel. "Now I'm taking her off Everest, and I just have to put her on a different planet. You can be a really talented and skilled basketball player and not win as much as she has and not become individually great as much as she has. She's the most coachable player I've ever been around. There's a reason why she keeps coming back better and better each year."

articles.title: Liberty make official inquiry into reset timeout dispute after overtime loss to Dream in WNBA semifinals
articles.summary: Breanna Stewart says officials told the Liberty they had no reset timeout when they actually did, sparking an inquiry after Atlanta Dream's OT win.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream moved within one victory of a WNBA Finals berth after outlasting the New York Liberty 101-98 in overtime Wednesday night to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the semifinal series. However, Game 2’s dramatic finish was overshadowed by controversy after New York star Breanna Stewart said officials incorrectly told the Liberty they did not have a reset timeout available in the closing seconds, even though the team still had one remaining. "This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end, and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with the reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart told reporters after the game. DREAM MOVE WITHIN ONE WIN OF FIRST WNBA FINALS APPEARANCE SINCE 2013 AFTER OVERTIME VICTORY Under league rules, each team is given two team timeouts and one reset timeout during overtime, allowing it to advance the ball without huddling on the sideline. Stewart continued later: "I asked Kevin [Fahy]. I said, 'Do we have a reset timeout?' And he said, 'I'm going to check at the table.' So then he looked to [crew chief] Fatou [Cissoko-Stephens], and she said, 'No.' So then he told me, 'No.'" A late New York turnover gave Atlanta an opportunity to put the game away. Angel Reese, the 2026 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year, went to the foul line and sank both free throws to extend the Dream’s lead to three points. The Liberty inbounded from under their own basket and got the ball to Stewart, but her desperation shot was no good as the clock ticked to triple zeros. WNBA'S OFFICIATING OVERHAUL IS ALREADY DRAWING COMPLAINTS FROM PLAYERS AND COACHES ONE WEEK INTO SEASON "Of course, who knows what happened to end the game," Stewart said. "But we would have had hopefully a better shot on our goal." Officials were not made available to members of the media until roughly two hours after the game. ESPN asked crew chief Fatou Cissoko-Stephens in the pool report why Stewart said she had been told the Liberty's reset timeout wasn't available. "Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," she said. The controversy has prompted the Liberty to formally inquire with the league about the situation, ESPN reported, citing sources. Asked whether he was unaware that the team had a reset timeout at their disposal, Liberty coach Chris DeMarco responded, "Yeah, same thing. They just said we didn't have it. Multiple staff members [were told]. It is what it is. We've got to demand more. But it is what it is." Dream coach Karl Smesko was also asked about the number of Liberty timeouts remaining. "I was, I thought they had a timeout left," Smesko said. "But they played it out the way they did. So I was expecting it to be advanced, but it wasn't, so we had to play it, and fortunately we were able to get the stop." Cissoko-Stephens added that the scorer’s table and stats staff keep up with the number of available timeouts, but emphasized that "teams are responsible for managing and tracking their timeout usage throughout the game." When the Liberty had possession in critical moments, they failed to capitalize on their opportunities. With less than 10 seconds remaining in overtime, Ionescu lost control of the ball while driving, sending it out of bounds. Ionescu took responsibility for the costly mistake. "I told them it was my fault," she said. "I took ownership for that. This loss is on me. I've got to take it on the chin, and I've got to be better." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Atlanta’s depth was on full display as six players scored in double figures, led by Reese and Jordin Canada with 23 points apiece. The Dream's leading scorer Allisha Gray sat out of the game due to a finger injury. The Liberty would have to overcome unprecedented odds to become the first team in WNBA history to erase a 2-0 deficit and win a best-of-five playoff series. Game 3 is scheduled for Friday night as the series shifts to Brooklyn, New York.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Nos hace falta un poco más de continuidad en el juego, más tiempo, conocernos mejor"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la victoria de su equipo ante el Partizan, la primera que consigue en la Euroliga
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la victoria de su equipo ante el Partizan, la primera que consigue en la Euroliga
articles.body: Pedro Martínez habló de lo que supone ocupar el banquillo de un equipo como el Real Madrid tras entrenar su primer partido como local con el conjunto blanco en la Euroliga, el cual terminó con victoria ante el Partizan de Belgrado por 86-76. "Estoy contento y feliz de entrenar a un equipo con el historial del Real Madrid, tremendamente orgulloso. Pero intento estar centrado en cómo ayudar al equipo y al club a que las cosas vayan bien, en asumir mis responsabilidades de la mejor manera que pueda. Intento apartarme todo lo que puedo de los aspectos sentimentales porque a veces juegan malas pasadas", dijo en rueda de prensa. Martínez consideró que la victoria es "importante" después de haber arrancado el curso en la máxima competición continental con tres tropiezos seguidos a domicilio y opinó que su equipo hizo una "muy buena" primera parte, aunque en la segunda no consiguió aguantar el ritmo, en parte porque el rival mejoró y porque todavía les está costando "tener un poco de continuidad en determinados básicos del juego". "Estoy muy contento con los jugadores, con la mentalidad. Hoy estaban súper concentrados, muy responsabilizados. Quieren, entrenan bien, tienen buena mentalidad y nos hace falta un poco más de continuidad en el juego. Nos hace falta más tiempo, conocernos mejor. Hoy me ha gustado la comunicación que han tenido los jugadores entre ellos, está muy bien, es algo que queremos que pase, que hablen, que se comuniquen. Eso nos irá haciendo mejorar, son pequeños aspectos del juego que a la larga acaban siendo muy importantes", declaró. "Está bien que el partido tenga dificultades y sobreponerse, a veces es mejor a que el partido venga de cara y ganes la primera parte de veinte o veinticinco. Superar adversidades es algo tremendamente positivo. Si pasa, ser capaces de volver a cambiar el ritmo y de que los jugadores hablen entre ellos, que volvamos a coger una distancia positiva también es bueno que pase porque no siempre va a venir todo de cara", indicó. Asimismo analizó la figura de Nick Smith Jr.: "Una pieza más para sumar en el engranaje, para darnos su talento y su mentalidad de querer mejorar. Estamos contentos con él, de cómo está adaptándose. No tiene experiencia en Europa y necesita un poco de periodo de adaptación. Está con una muy buena mentalidad y esperamos que siga mejorando y que nos ayude".

articles.title: Ex-College Basketball Player Kerr Kriisa Admits Demanding $9,000 From Victim in Fraud Scheme
articles.summary: CLARKSBURG, W.Va. (AP) — Former college basketball player Kerr Kriisa admitted Thursday to demanding $9,000 from a victim as part of a fraud scheme.
articles.body:
CLARKSBURG, W.Va. (AP) — Former college basketball player Kerr Kriisa admitted Thursday to demanding $9,000 from a victim as part of a fraud scheme.

Kriisa pleaded guilty to one federal count of wire fraud as part of a plea agreement, U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey announced in a news release.

Last February, Kriisa posed as a made-up person named "Irene" and emailed a person asking for money in order to avoid litigation and publicity concerning a financial dispute, according to the plea agreement.

"Financial fraud is not a game, and those who choose to deceive and exploit others will be held accountable," Harvey, the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of West Virginia, said in a statement.

Kriisa, a 6-foot-3 guard from Estonia , faces up to two years in prison. Sentencing was set for Dec. 22.

Kriisa's attorney, federal public defender Richard Walker, declined to comment on the plea agreement.

Kriisa led the Pac-12 in assists during two seasons at Arizona, where he began his college career in 2020. Kriisa was suspended for the first nine games of his lone season at West Virginia after admitting he received impermissible benefits while at Arizona. He transferred to Kentucky in 2024 but was limited to nine games with a foot injury. He spent his final year of eligibility at Cincinnati, where he started 12 games before suffering a separated shoulder.

The 25-year-old Kriisa was indicted in June on five counts of wire fraud in what prosecutors alleged was a $2.2 million scheme dating back to at least 2022. The indictment alleged Kriisa repeatedly sought payments from two victims. At times, he instructed one of them to transfer money to the other under false pretenses. He also had signed an agreement in April 2025 promising to repay one of the victims $100,000 by February 2026 but never did, prosecutors said.

From 2022 through June 2 of this year, Kriisa posed as other people, including his own mother, and falsely claimed that he and his family urgently needed money to deal with an emergency, the indictment said.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark left off 19 WNBA MVP ballots despite historic season as A’ja Wilson wins fifth award
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark became the first WNBA player to average 20 points and eight assists in a season, yet 19 voters left her off MVP ballots entirely.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark received one first-place vote for WNBA MVP after producing a season nobody in the league had managed before. And that might not even be the most ridiculous part of the results. Nineteen voters didn't put her on their ballots at all. The WNBA announced Thursday that A’ja Wilson won her record fifth MVP award, receiving 65 of the 74 first-place votes from a panel of sportswriters and broadcasters. Minnesota rookie Olivia Miles finished second, followed by Indiana’s Kelsey Mitchell and Clark. CAITLIN CLARK SAYS SHE BLOCKS SOCIAL MEDIA HATE AND ENJOYS HOSTILE WNBA ROAD CROWDS Clark appeared on 55 ballots, receiving one first-place vote, six second-place votes, 20 third-place votes, 16 fourth-place votes and 12 fifth-place votes. She finished with 212 points, well behind Miles’ 442 and Mitchell’s 287. Wilson had an outstanding season and a compelling case to win. But apparently, more than a quarter of the voters watched Clark this year and decided five other players deserved recognition ahead of her. I'd love to hear those explanations. Caitlin Clark’s historic season deserved more consideration Clark averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game, becoming the first WNBA player to finish a season averaging at least 20 points and eight assists. Combining her own baskets and free throws with the points teammates scored from her assists, Clark created an average of 41.2 points per game. According to the WNBA’s own end-of-season review, that was the highest average in league history. That's a useful place to start a conversation about offensive value, especially when her teammate finished ahead of her in MVP voting. There's a compelling case that Mitchell benefited from Clark far more than vice versa. After all, Mitchell just completed her ninth WNBA season. In her six years with Indiana prior to Clark's arrival, Mitchell averaged 16.4 points per game. In the three seasons since the Fever drafted Clark, Mitchell has averaged 21.4 points, including a career-high 24.7 points this season. Clark also had five games with at least 30 points and 10 assists this season. Every other player in WNBA history combined has four. Read that again. Read that again. Caitlin Clark did something five times in one season that every other player combined has done four times in WNBA regular-season history. Her best performance came against Seattle on July 17, when she scored 45 points and had 10 assists. It was the first 40-point, 10-assist game the WNBA had ever seen. And those spectacular nights were backed by sustained production. Clark recorded 13 games with at least 20 points and 10 assists, nearly one-third of her 40 appearances. She finished with 891 points and 333 assists, becoming the first player to reach 800 points and 300 assists in a season. Then there's the team success. Indiana averaged a league-record 96 points per game. Clark’s ability to score while creating opportunities for her teammates helped make that possible. Apparently, some voters found all of that easier to overlook than others. Miles averaged 19.8 points and six assists while helping Minnesota finish with the league’s best record. Although it's worth noting that Minnesota also finished with the league’s best record in 2025, before Miles entered the league. Mitchell scored a league-record 1,086 points. That's impressive, but Clark helped create those scoring opportunities through both her passing and the defensive attention she draws. Wilson, meanwhile, averaged 26.2 points and 9.4 rebounds, led the league in points and blocks per game, and helped Las Vegas win 31 games. Her ability to dominate at both ends gives voters plenty of reasons to put her first and, honestly, she probably deserved to win. But choosing Wilson and leaving Clark outside the top five are very different judgments. WNBA media has earned the scrutiny The award was decided by sportswriters and broadcasters. Given how some prominent members of that industry have covered Clark, skepticism about their judgment shouldn't surprise anyone. Too much of the coverage treats her popularity as something that needs a racial explanation before anyone can simply appreciate her basketball. In May, Cari Champion said about Clark: "I don’t like you. I don’t like the way you behave on the court." By September, Champion was calling Clark an "avatar for people who want to spread hate." In July, Nancy Armour argued that Clark’s reactions to officiating endangered Black and queer players, even invoking Emmett Till. Even this week, Charlotte Wilder wanted "something a little more forceful" from Clark about the alleged treatment of Black WNBA players, despite acknowledging she had already spoken out. That coverage reflects a preference for a story in which Black players need defending and Clark needs to constantly apologize for her mere existence. Her performance too often becomes secondary to what commentators believe her popularity represents. Sportswriters, commentators and broadcasters are entitled to their opinions (as bad as they often are). Those examples don't tell us who left Clark off a ballot, but they help explain why fans might question the media’s judgment. SOCIAL MEDIA WAS NOT LOVING CAITLIN CLARK GETTING SNUBBED BY TV NETWORK'S MVP GRAPHIC And questioning their judgment doesn't require rooting against Wilson. She received only four Defensive Player of the Year votes while Angel Reese received 46 and won the award in a landslide. I thought Wilson deserved considerably more support in that race, but as I argued at the time, the media loves to trumpet Reese as a star and they needed a reason to prop her up. The standard should be consistent: evaluate what the players actually did, and be prepared to defend the result. Clark deserved to finish higher in MVP voting To be clear, Clark’s popularity doesn't entitle her to an MVP award. But it's not like her play didn't warrant consideration as the league's most valuable player. There is room to disagree about how much weight to give defense, turnovers, scoring efficiency or a team’s record. Reasonable people can disagree about where Clark belonged behind Wilson, but leaving the Fever superstar outside the top five is borderline malpractice. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Nineteen voters decided a historic combination of scoring and playmaking wasn't worth even a fifth-place vote. That doesn't prove that they simply don't like Caitlin Clark and don't want her to succeed, but it certainly raises the question. If those 19 voters have a basketball explanation for leaving Clark off their ballots, they should make it public immediately.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Fever set a TV ratings bar the WNBA semifinal openers could not come close to reaching
articles.summary: Indiana Fever regular-season games averaged 2.32 million viewers on major networks, more than double Sunday's WNBA semifinal openers on ABC and NBC.
articles.body: The Indiana Fever's regular-season games on major broadcast networks averaged more than twice the audience of the WNBA semifinal openers on Oct. 4. And those playoff games were on ABC and NBC. An OutKick review of Indiana's 10 regular-season games on ABC, CBS and NBC found an average audience of approximately 2.32 million viewers. The two semifinal openers averaged about 1.16 million. CAITLIN CLARK SENDS WNBA ALL-STAR RATINGS SOARING AS 3-POINT CONTEST AUDIENCE FALLS WITHOUT HER That gave Indiana an average audience approximately 100% larger, a difference of nearly 1.16 million viewers per game. New York–Atlanta's Game 1 averaged 1.2 million viewers on ABC, ESPN told OutKick. Las Vegas–Golden State averaged 1.12 million on NBC and Peacock, according to figures NBC supplied to OutKick. Just one Sunday earlier, Indiana's first-round opener against Las Vegas averaged 2.11 million viewers on ABC. That Sept. 27 game also aired opposite the NFL, yet drew approximately 76% more viewers than New York–Atlanta's semifinal opener on the same network a week later. The stakes went up, but the audience went down. That's a pretty good answer to anyone still wondering how much Caitlin Clark means to the WNBA's television business. Even Indiana's smallest major-network audience was bigger The 2.32 million average covers four Fever games on ABC, four on CBS and two on NBC, using reported audiences from the regular season. The NBC figures include Peacock, just as the Aces–Valkyries playoff figure does. Seven of those 10 Fever games exceeded two million viewers. Every one of the 10 drew a larger audience than either semifinal opener. The smallest was Indiana's May 30 game at Portland on CBS, which Sports Media Watch reported at nearly 1.3 million. Clark had one of her worst games of the season, scoring just 6 points on 1-for-7 shooting, and the Fever trailed by as many as 26 points. Think about that, though. A regular-season game against Portland in May, where Clark played just 22 minutes in a blowout loss, drew more viewers than either game to open the WNBA semifinals in October. WNBA WANTS A BIGGER STORY THAN CAITLIN CLARK, BUT TV RATINGS KEEP POINTING BACK TO HER At the other end, Indiana's Aug. 23 game against Chicago averaged 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock. Its July 12 game against Las Vegas drew 2.64 million on those same platforms. New York offers another useful comparison. The Liberty's two regular-season meetings with Indiana on CBS each drew over 2.5 million viewers. Sunday's Liberty–Dream semifinal opener drew 1.2 million on ABC. Angel Reese, who now plays for Atlanta, famously insisted in 2024 that people watch women's basketball "because of me too." Well, New York facing Clark's Fever in the regular season drew more than twice the audience of New York facing Reese's Dream in the final four. The numbers show that Reese isn't much of a television draw, as Dream playoff games are right in line with the other non-Clark games and, in some cases, actually worse. Atlanta's first-round clincher averaged 1.2 million viewers on ESPN, below the 1.4 million for Dallas–Golden State on the same network that night. WNBA semifinal numbers are strong, but Fever numbers are stronger This isn't to say that this is bad news for the WNBA because it isn't. Before Clark arrived in 2024, the league hadn't had a game average one million viewers since 2008. Consistently clearing that mark represents real progress. WNBA MEDIA RIGHTS DEAL BALLOONS PAST $3 BILLION AFTER ADDING NEW BROADCAST PARTNERS TO 11-YEAR PORTFOLIO Plus, the two semifinal openers averaged around 10% more viewers than last year's pair. Sports Media Watch ranked them second and third among semifinal Game 1 audiences since the league adopted its current semifinal format in 2016. The only opener ahead of them? Last year's Fever–Aces game, which drew 1.4 million on ABC even with Clark sidelined by injury. That's encouraging for the league, and another reminder of the audience Indiana has built. Even during this year's regular season, the Fever drew 1.57 million against Los Angeles on CBS on June 27 without Clark playing. There is an audience for the Fever beyond simply checking whether Clark is in uniform that day. The WNBA would benefit enormously from building that kind of interest around more of its teams. As I reported earlier this week, even Indiana's least-watched first-round game, its 1.42 million-viewer appearance on Prime Video, outdrew every non-Fever first-round game. That streaming-exclusive audience also exceeded both semifinal openers on broadcast television. Fans found the Fever wherever their games aired. The remaining teams now have the opportunity to give those viewers a reason to keep watching. I'll be interested to see whether the audiences build as the series progress. For now, though, the remaining teams are trying to match numbers the Fever were putting up in May.

articles.summary: Before entering the BIG3, Jannero Pargo played 11 seasons in the NBA, spending three of those with the Charlotte Bobcats/Hornets.
articles.body:
After point guard Ramon Sessions went down with an injury during the 2012-13 season, the Charlotte Bobcats brought in veteran guard Jannero Pargo on a 10-day contract. Pargo, a former undrafted prospect out of Arkansas, played well enough to earn a contract for the remainder of the 2012-13 season and would later re-sign to stay in Charlotte.

Pargo played parts of three seasons with Charlotte in total, remaining on the roster as the franchise shifted from the Bobcats to the Hornets. In 56 contests, Pargo averaged 5.9 points, 0.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 0.5 steals. Throughout his 11-year NBA career, Pargo played in 499 games, and his best season came during the 2006-07 campaign with New Orleans, where he tallied 9.2 points, 2.2 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 0.6 steals, suiting up in all 82 contests. Pargo's brother, Jeremy Pargo, also played in the NBA.

articles.title: ESPN video shows Breanna Stewart asking ref about reset timeout at end of Liberty’s Game 2 loss
articles.summary: NEW YORK — In footage showing part of a disputed interaction between Breanna Stewart and an official, ESPN video shows the New York Liberty forward asking a...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — In footage showing part of a disputed interaction between Breanna Stewart and an official, ESPN video shows the New York Liberty forward asking a referee about a reset timeout near the end of Wednesday night's overtime WNBA playoff loss to the Atlanta Dream.

In the video, which aired Thursday on ESPN's "NBA Today," Stewart can be seen turning toward official Kevin Fahy and is heard asking , "Do we have a reset?" But it is unclear from the video or audio whether Fahy, shown behind Stewart's position between free throws by Atlanta's Angel Reese, acknowledged Stewart or answered her question. He appears to be communicating toward the scorer's table.

In a postgame pool report, lead official Fatou Cissoko-Stephens said Stewart was told the Liberty had a reset timeout, contradicting Stewart's comments immediately after the game in which she said she was told the opposite.

The Liberty had one reset timeout remaining, meaning they could advance the ball to mid-court down three points to the Dream with 4.3 seconds left, but they did not use it. Instead, New York inbounded the ball from the baseline, and Stewart's desperation heave missed in the 101-98 loss.

"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with a reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said late Wednesday night. "Yeah, OK, I kind of got a good look at the end, but would just love to have some clarity on that situation."

The Liberty have filed an inquiry with the league to look into the situation, according to a source familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they weren't permitted to speak publicly on the matter. The league received Liberty's inquiry and is looking into the matter, according to another source familiar with the process who spoke on condition of anonymity because they also weren't permitted to speak publicly.

After the game, Stewart said Fahy told her he was checking on the Liberty's available reset timeouts and asked Cissoko-Stephens before telling Stewart the Liberty did not have one. New York coach Chris DeMarco also said officials told them New York did not have a reset timeout.

But in the pool report, Cissoko-Stephens said there was no "direct communication" between the officials and the Liberty's coaching staff.

"Stewart was standing behind referee (Kevin) Fahy when he confirmed with his (officiating) partner between (Angel) Reese's penalty free throws that the Liberty did indeed have a reset (timeout) remaining," Cissoko-Stephens told reporters after the game.

Dream coach Karl Smesko said he was aware the Liberty had a reset timeout and expected them to use it. Instead, the final possession was Stewart heaving the ball from halfcourt as time expired. The Liberty's bench appeared confused during the last seconds of the game.

The WNBA rulebook states that each team is entitled to one reset timeout in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter. Teams also receive one reset timeout in the final two minutes of overtime.

The Dream took a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five game series, putting them one game away from making their first WNBA Finals appearance since 2013. The series continues in New York on Friday with a must-win Game 3 for the Liberty, though no team in WNBA history has ever come back after going down 2-0 in a five-game series.

articles.title: Warriors Brandin Podziemski Gets Major $70M Contract Extension Update
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are predicted to agree to a $70 million Brandin Podziemski contract extension for the guard after a career-year. The post Warriors...
articles.body:
Chatter throughout the NBA offseason surrounding the Golden State Warriors has been about a Brandin Podziemski contract extension. But despite general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. stating a new deal is a top priority for the team, it still hasn't come.

Podziemski is in the final season of his rookie contract, on the books for $5.6 million this year with the Warriors. Both sides have openly discussed a new deal, but so far, no ink has been put to paper.

Golden State still has a bit of time to agree on a Podziemski contract extension in an agreement that works for both sides, and according to a new report, the Warriors guard could be in line for a big payday very soon.

Brandin Podziemski Contract Extension Predicted To Be For $70 Million

Reporting for ClutchPoints, NBA insider Brett Siegel predicts Podziemski's next deal with the Warriors will be for roughly $70 million over four seasons. The young guard, about to enter his fourth NBA season, has shown flashes of being a high-level player, and he's been a consistent-enough staple in Golden State's rotation over the past few years to earn him that type of money.

" As reported throughout the offseason by ClutchPoints , Golden State's sweet spot on a new contract with Podziemski is somewhere in the $16 million to $18 million range in terms of annual average value," he wrote. Of course, an AAV of $16 million would essentially be a contract at the mid-level exception for Podziemski."

Last season, Podziemski was one of 18 NBA players to appear in all 82 games. He averaged 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. The 23-year-old was the Warriors' main guard at several points last year with Jimmy Butler and Stephen Curry out with injuries, but as Siegel wrote, getting more than mid-level money doesn't look like a realistic scenario.

"On the other side of things, we've reported that Podziemski and his camp would be wanting something more in the $20 million to $24 million range. While he and his representation would obviously want to try and maximize a contract extension, these figures are a little unrealistic for Podziemski at this juncture."

But still, there remain questions about Podziemski's game as a whole. He isn't the biggest, strongest, or fastest, and has some tendencies that might make it a difficult decision for the Warriors to hand him $70 million in a new contract extension.

"That is why there is a wide belief that an extension for Podziemski would fall in the $16 million to $18 million range, which would help the Warriors immensely and still give them max contract cap space next summer," he added.

Though Siegel's $70 million number was just a prediction, there's a real chance Podziemski could get that type of money. Both sides still have time to agree on a deal, but with the season about to begin, getting both sides to finalize the terms as soon as possible would be best for everyone involved.

Is Golden State Close To Getting A Deal Done?

As mentioned, Dunleavy has said on multiple occasions that a Podziemski contract extension is a top priority for the Warriors.

"We really value Brandin. He's a player who, for all the things he does well, most importantly, he impacts winning. When he's on the court, we're a better team. So anytime you've got a guy like that, you want to be able to keep him around," Dunleavy said over the summer.

"Obviously, we have multiple ways to do it through an extension and restricted free agency and all that, but we prefer to get it done sooner rather than later. We really like Brandin. He's done a terrific job for us, and he's a big part of our program."

Both the player and the team have obviously still yet to agree on a number, but if they weren't too far off, one would think it would be fairly easy for an agreement to have already happened. That tends to indicate Golden State and Podziemski are looking at very different price tags for what he should be owed.

Regardless, as NBA insider Marc Stein recently reported , a timeline might be emerging on when a contract extension could get signed, and that could be before October 19 deadline when rosters for the new are finalized

"Regarding Podziemski specifically: Word relayed to The Stein Line this week is that both sides want to get a deal done… but that is obviously dependent on beating the ticking clock," Stein wrote.

Podziemki himself spoke about his incoming Warriors contract extension at Media Day, stating that he isn't worried about a deal getting done.

"I don't let that interfere with our team dynamic. I know what they want from me is just to be the best version of myself I can be. And the contract stuff, my agent and Mike (Dunleavy Jr.) and them will handle," he said. "I never get caught up thinking that it's a contract possibility, this, that, I don't…When it's supposed to happen, it's going to happen. And I'm a firm believer with that."

Though Siegel's $70 million Podziemski contract extension prediction is one number, other estimates on the Warriors guard's new deal have been anywhere from $60 million to $100 million.

Without Moses Moody , Butler, and perhaps Kristaps Porzingis , Podziemski, already coming off a career year, will likely have even more responsibility this season, which could make it more likely he signs for more money.

No deal has happened yet, and though the Warriors have just days left to agree to terms with the 23-year-old, signs point to it getting done soon, with an exact number still yet to be decided.

articles.title: Mitchell Robinson Takes Apparent Shot at Knicks After Celtics Move
articles.summary: Mitchell Robinson raises eyebrows with comments about the Knicks' playing restrictions after joining the rival Boston Celtics. The post Mitchell Robinson Tak...
articles.body:
spent eight seasons in New York, but it took only a few weeks in Boston for the former Knicks center to suggest that his old team had been holding him back.

Robinson, who signed with the Celtics this summer after helping the Knicks win an NBA championship, believes he will have more freedom to play than he did during his final years at Madison Square Garden.

His comments about playing back-to-back games sounded like a pointed criticism of the Knicks' cautious approach to his health.

"Oh, nah, it ain't going to be the same in Boston [as it was with the Knicks]," Robinson told Knicks Fan TV . "I'll be able to play back-to-backs."

For a player who spent much of his Knicks career dealing with injuries, the possibility of playing without scheduled restrictions clearly carries some significance.

"So, I'm very excited for that, it's been a long time coming," Robinson continued. "Now I can go out there and play basketball and not have to worry about not playing this game. Just go out there with a free mind and just hoop."

Mitchell Robinson Appears Frustrated With Knicks' Cautious Approach

Robinson did not directly accuse the Knicks of mishandling his health. But his emphasis on finally being able to play freely suggests he wasn't entirely comfortable with the restrictions imposed during his final seasons in New York.

The Knicks had good reason to be careful.

Robinson underwent multiple ankle procedures and missed significant stretches of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons. His injury history prompted the organization to limit his appearances in back-to-back games, hoping to keep him healthy for the playoffs.

Robinson appeared in 60 regular-season games in 2025-26, his highest total in four seasons, averaging 5.7 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.2 blocks.

More importantly, he remained available during New York's championship run, providing the offensive rebounding and interior defense that made him valuable alongside Karl-Anthony Towns .

The Knicks could reasonably argue that their cautious handling helped preserve Robinson for the games that mattered most.

Robinson, however, appears eager to leave that arrangement behind.

His confidence does not necessarily mean the Celtics will abandon workload management. Boston has yet to publicly commit to playing him on consecutive nights.

Robinson Faces Familiar Challenge With Celtics

Boston signed Robinson to a three-year, $47.4 million contract, ending his eight-year association with New York.

The Celtics are hoping his physicality and rebounding will strengthen their frontcourt, but they also inherit another weakness that Knicks fans know well.

Robinson is a career 50.8% free-throw shooter, one of the poorest marks in NBA history .

Opponents frequently exploited that weakness with intentional fouls, including Boston under coach Joe Mazzulla.

The strategy became known as "Hack-a-Mitch."

Robinson says he has changed his approach at the foul line.

"Back in the day I was just like more, get it over with. Now I'm actually focusing in on it, locking in, and getting it in the air," Robinson told The Boston Globe .

Robinson is expected to make his Celtics preseason debut Thursday night against the Cleveland Cavaliers .

His comments about New York add intrigue to his fresh start, particularly given the rivalry between the two Atlantic Division teams.

But the Knicks' decision to protect Robinson wasn't made without justification. His availability during their championship run offered a compelling argument for patience.

Robinson believes he can handle a heavier workload in Boston.

The coming season will reveal whether the Celtics share that confidence — and whether his body can support it.

articles.title: Pair of Florida volleyball stars named to Player of the Year Watch List
articles.summary: Taylor Parks and Alec Rothe will represent Florida volleyball on the 2026 AVCA Division I Player of the Year Watch List.
articles.body:
Taylor Parks and Alec Rothe will represent No. 5 Florida volleyball on the 2026 AVCA Division I Player of the Year Watch List, presented by Nike Volleyball, as the organization announced the additions to the list on Thursday afternoon.

Parks, a third-year setter, helps direct a potent Gators offense that is hitting .291, the second-best mark in the Southeastern Conference and ninth in the NCAA. The Clearwater, Florida, native ranks in the top 100 nationally in multiple categories, including assists per set (32nd, 10.30) and total assists (90th, 474).

She also plays a critical role on defense, averaging 2.22 digs per set. Against No. 3 Kentucky, Parks recorded a career-high six kills on 10 attempts, hitting .500.

Rothe has established herself as one of the nation's best middle blockers. The third-year Dublin, Ohio, native leads the SEC with a .449 hitting percentage, which is seventh nationally. She also averages 1.29 blocks per set — fourth in the conference and 49th in the NCAA — along with 3.13 points and 2.42 kills per set.

Against No. 5 Wisconsin in early September, Rothe posted 11 blocks, which tied for ninth in a single match in school history, and her 10 block assists tied for sixth.

The duo is among 16 athletes added to the list, joining 30 who were named to the Preseason Watch List in July. The AVCA will release the semifinalists in mid-November and the finalists in December. The Player of the Year will be named at the AVCA Awards Banquet on Friday, Dec. 18, in San Antonio.
